data.title: Build a checked analysis inside Excel with Copilot
data.summary: Plan the analysis, create workbook-native formulas and reconcile results against the existing public variance example.

facts.text: Copilot in Excel offers edit, plan and chat modes on supported Windows, Mac and web clients. Edit mode changes the workbook; chat can analyze without editing. Availability depends on the account and client.

sources.title: Get started with Copilot in Excel

prerequisites: An eligible Copilot-enabled Excel account and supported client.
A review copy of a structured table with named columns and agreed totals.
steps: Open the existing workbook, or import the linked public sample into a disposable workbook. Record row counts and scope.
Open Copilot in Excel and choose plan or chat mode for the first request. Specify tables, columns and intended output.
Inspect its proposed grouping, filters and formulas. Ask for explicit entity, period, currency and zero-budget handling.
Use edit mode on the review copy to create formulas and a compact results table; inspect the actual cells.
Recalculate and compare detail rows and totals with the approved reference. Compute total percentage from totals, not averaged row percentages.
Save the checked workbook and retain the prompt, filters and unresolved issues.
data.output: A workbook-native analysis with visible formulas, scope and a reconciled results table.
validation: Filters exclude the wrong entity/period/currency; detail sums reconcile to the total.
Zero budget is undefined for percentage variance, while missing data is flagged separately.
limitations: Copilot was not run by Sintra; only the existing public reference calculation is tested.
Licensing and mode names can vary by rollout. Do not infer that an available chat pane can edit the workbook.
data.prompt: Inspect [table] in plan mode first. For [entity, period, currency], propose a formula-based Actual versus Budget table and explain zero and missing-budget handling. After review, create it in this copy. Show formulas, detail and total variance, and total percentage calculated from the total budget. Reconcile to [reference totals] and list any mismatches.

replication.environment: Copilot in Excel: Windows, Mac or web
replication.useWhen: Explore a structured finance table with formulas you can inspect.

inputs.name: Finance table
inputs.detail: Entity, fiscalPeriod, currency, product, scenario and amountCents; retain integer cents and text periods.

inputs.name: Reference
inputs.detail: Reuse LAB-FPNA-01's existing public dataset and expected results.

launch: Download the practice CSV and import it into a disposable workbook as a table.
Select Copilot, then plan/chat before enabling edits to the copy.

practice.task: Analyze Demo Europe, 2026-09, EUR using the existing sample. No Power BI connection is required.
practice.expected: Budget EUR 21,000; actual EUR 19,650; variance −EUR 1,350; total −6.428571%; New offer percentage undefined. Exclude two out-of-scope rows.

acceptanceTests.scenario: Another entity and period are present
acceptanceTests.expected: Exclude them explicitly; totals remain the reference totals.

acceptanceTests.scenario: A budget is zero or missing
acceptanceTests.expected: Distinguish undefined percentage from missing evidence; do not convert either silently to 0%.

troubleshooting.action: Review the account/client capability; use suggested formulas manually and label the route accurately.
Check filters, numeric types and denominator; recompute from aggregate amounts.
